children: Swiss inflation rose again last month to reach its highest level in almost three years, driven by the continued increase in imported energy prices amid enduring uncertainty over the outcome of the war in the Middle East.
Annual inflation was 1.5% in October, compared with 1.0% in the prior month, notching its strongest point since December 2023, Switzerland's statistics office said Tuesday.

Oil prices continued to climb last month, pushing up the price of gas at the pump. Inflation is above the midpoint of the Swiss National Bank's 0% to 2% target range for the first time since August 2024.

But unlike other central banks that have raised rates in recent months in response to the climb in energy prices, the SNB is expected by investors to keep its key rate on hold until well into next year.
Economists tend to see Switzerland as less exposed to higher energy prices from the war in Iran, given its more diversified energy mix that includes Alpine hydroelectric dams and nuclear power.

title: Swiss Inflation Jumps to Highest Since 2023 on Imported Energy Costs
